title: OpenAI cuts its funding round by $10 billion as the AI stock rout spooks investors
summary: OpenAI is now seeking up to $20 billion in its latest round, down from a target of about $30 billion, CNBC confirmed on Saturday after the Financial Times first reported the cut. The FT said the round values OpenAI at $1.25 trillion after the money comes in, down from the $1.4 trillion it was aiming for, and that some investors trimmed their commitments ahead of a Friday deadline. Investors from the United Arab Emirates are leading alongside Coatue, CNBC reported. The round is still open, so the figures could change, and it lands the same week AI stocks sank on worries that data center spending won’t pay off.

title: S&P 500 futures bounce back after a bruising October, with Apple and Palantir reporting tonight
summary: U.S. stock futures pointed to a rebound this morning, Investing.com reported: Nasdaq 100 futures were up 0.84% and S&P 500 futures up 0.6% by 6:10 a.m. ET. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 5% in October as AI stocks were repriced, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.9% and the Dow gained 1.7%. Apple and Palantir report after the closing bell today, and Tuesday brings the midterm elections and AMD’s results, with the October jobs report on Friday.

title: Apple passes Nvidia to become the world’s most valuable company again
summary: Apple reclaimed the title of world’s most valuable company on Friday, Bloomberg reported. Its shares fell 1.2%, leaving it worth $5.03 trillion, while Nvidia sank 4.2% to $4.93 trillion amid worries about AI spending. Apple has kept a lid on capital spending, which has helped make it the best performer of the Magnificent Seven this year, up 27%. It’s the first time Apple has passed Nvidia since briefly doing so in late July, and Apple reports its quarterly results after the bell today, the first under CEO John Ternus.

title: AMD reports Tuesday, the first big chipmaker test since Friday’s rout
summary: Advanced Micro Devices reports third-quarter results after the close on Tuesday, November 3, with a call at 5 p.m. ET. AMD guided revenue to about $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million, which it says is about 41% more than a year earlier, with a non-GAAP gross margin near 56%, MoverTape reported. AMD shares fell nearly 11% on Friday as Intel’s forecast dragged chipmakers down, Investing.com noted, so investors want proof that its data center chips are still selling. Arista and Supermicro report the same evening, and Arm and Qualcomm follow on Wednesday.

title: ChatGPT will fold Work into Chat in December, with one shared token budget
summary: Starting in December, ChatGPT’s Plus, Pro, and Business plans will share a single token budget across ChatGPT and Codex as OpenAI moves Work’s agent features into the main app, according to an updated OpenAI support page reported by The Decoder. Bigger models and harder tasks use up the budget faster; when it runs out, users can wait for the reset, upgrade, or buy credits. Chats with Instant models won’t count against it, and you’ll be able to check your balance and reset time in Settings.

title: SenseTime’s open Loop-9B runs the same layers twice to think deeper without getting bigger
summary: SenseTime’s SenseNova team released SenseNova-Loop-9B-Preview, an open-weight model that reads text and images and is built for long documents, coding, and tool use. A block of 24 of its 32 layers runs twice in a row with the same weights, so it does 56 layers of work while storing only 32, and a technique called two-stream mHC manages how information flows through the loop. It was trained on sequences of up to 262,144 tokens and ships under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face.

title: Idol turns one picture into a 3D object in seconds, including the sides you can’t see
summary: Sperid Labs released Idol, an open model that turns a single image of an object into a 3D Gaussian splat of up to about a million points, saved as a standard .ply file, and fills in the sides the picture never showed. It removes the background on its own, needs 7.2 GB of graphics memory at peak, and on a top data center GPU makes an object in about 3.4 seconds; on an RTX 4090 it takes about 19 seconds. Sperid’s own benchmark puts it ahead of TRELLIS and TripoSplat on most measures.

title: DeepSeek open-sources a coding agent that takes requests and comes back with pull requests
summary: DeepSeek’s Harness team open-sourced dsh-superagent, a research prototype that takes development requests through GitHub, and optionally the Feishu chat app, works on each in its own session and folder, and returns results such as pull requests to the original conversation, TechNode reported. It is set up around a single GitHub repository and includes a web panel showing what needs a human’s attention. The team says it grew out of its own daily workflow; it’s a prototype, not an official product, and it’s available under the MIT license.

title: Google DeepMind’s PlanAssist cuts the time planners spend on home extension applications by up to 58%
summary: PlanAssist, an AI planning tool built with Gemini by Google DeepMind with the UK government, Google Cloud, and Faculty, is expanding to 12 more English councils for a 12-month trial on live applications. In pilots at Barnet, Camden, and Dorset, it cut the average time officers spent assessing householder applications such as loft conversions and extensions by 58%, and officers approved more than 70% of its draft reports with no edits. It checks documents, drawings, heritage rules, and local policies and drafts cited reports, but planning officers keep the final say on every decision.

title: Annoyed at learning about a school board vote secondhand, a student built an AI tool so no one else misses one
summary: Ronit Singh, a student at Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology in Virginia, only learned his school board had changed its cellphone rules when a friend told him. So he and two friends built Civic Cycle, a free website that spots newly published school board agendas, summarizes the meetings with Claude, and has a person review every summary “because we know that some people don’t trust AI fully,” WTOP reported. It covers Fairfax, Loudoun, Arlington, and Prince William counties and can send email alerts on topics you follow.

title: A student’s AI wearable for people with low vision wins Canada’s top youth innovation prize
summary: Surya Narayan Santhakumar won the Grand Award and $10,000 at the 2026 Canada Youth Innovation Competition for VisionIQ, an AI-powered wearable for people with visual impairments, Victoria Media reported. He was one of 45 students in grades 7 to 12 who shared $100,000 in prizes; other winners built a tiny text-to-speech model, a transit-delay predictor, a cancer-screening platform, and an air-quality warning system. The competition ran for nearly six months on the theme of AI agents and future living.

title: Tonight: a bluegrass jam at Cité des Arts
summary: Bring an instrument or just come listen: Cité des Arts, at 109 Vine Street downtown, hosts a bluegrass jam tonight at 6:30 p.m., according to The Acadiana Advocate’s weekly live music listings. Charley G’s Seafood Grill also has live music tonight at 6 p.m.

title: Tuesday: Election Day in Lafayette Parish, with Senate, House, and local races on the ballot
summary: Tuesday, November 3, is the open congressional general and open primary election in Lafayette Parish, according to the Clerk of Court. The ballot includes U.S. Senator and U.S. Representative, plus district judges, the district attorney, justices of the peace and constables, and, depending on where you live, Lafayette City Court and School Board District 2, or mayor and council races in Broussard, Carencro, Duson, Scott, and Youngsville. Sample ballots are on the Clerk’s site, and the Registrar of Voters is at (337) 291-7140.

title: Tuesday night: try five minutes of stand-up at the Oof. Comedy Hour open mic
summary: Cité des Arts runs its Oof. Comedy Hour open mic every Tuesday at 8 p.m. at 109 Vine Street. Sign up by 7:45 p.m. to get a slot, or just come to laugh.

title: Wednesday: practice your French at Table Française, then stay for the Cajun jam at the Blue Moon
summary: Alliance Française de Lafayette hosts Table Française at the Blue Moon Saloon, 215 East Convent Street, from 6:30 to 8 p.m. on Wednesday, with no RSVP required. The Blue Moon’s Cajun jam follows at 8 p.m., according to The Acadiana Advocate’s listings.

title: Friday: free Downtown Alive! with the Pine Leaf Boys, plus science fun for kids
summary: Downtown Alive!, Acadiana’s longest-running free concert series, features the Pine Leaf Boys with opening act the Josh Mendoza Experience on Friday from 6 to 8:30 p.m. at Parc Sans Souci, 201 East Vermilion Street. The Children’s Museum of Acadiana brings CMA on the Go!, with hands-on science, math, and creativity activities for kids. Leave ice chests at home; drinks and food are sold on site.

title: Saturday: the dance collective GROCO performs ‘Sealed on the Third Floor’ at Cité des Arts
summary: Lafayette GROCO, a project-based dance collective working to grow opportunities for professional dancers across Louisiana, performs “Sealed on the Third Floor” at Cité des Arts on Saturday from 5:30 to 7 p.m., with tickets through Givebutter. Earlier that day, Cité des Arts holds its weekly Essentials of Tai Chi class at 8 a.m., and Alliance Française opens its library for coffee from 10 a.m. to noon at 735 Jefferson Street.
